description: UNOS feature ledger (ADR-0203): the user-visible features and the planned changes, each with the steps that verify it. passes turns true only after every step passed as a user scenario: the tests in verified_by assert each step, the E2E specs on the local stand-in cover the steps in the web UI, and an entry whose steps make a host-level change (GLOSSARY.md) has also passed a device check and a re-check after a reboot of the deployed tree (ADR-0018). A pass also needs a reviewer in a fresh context who tried to refute the change, with each finding fixed or recorded (ADR-0017). A failing re-check, or a step that its tests do not assert as written, sets passes back to false. A pass changes only passes, verified_by and notes; changing a description or the steps, or dropping an entry, needs a new ADR that names the entry's id, and a changed entry lists that ADR in adr. supervisor/tests/test_feature_list.py compares the ledger with the one at the branch's merge base with main, where an ADR is new when its number is not in that base's docs/adr, and skips the comparison while that base has no ledger: until the ledger is merged into main neither a local run nor CI catches a dropped or reworded entry (ci.ledger-changes-checked). The feature-pass skill carries one entry per pass.

features.description: Issues on GitHub are triaged with the labels needs-triage, needs-info, ready-for-agent, ready-for-human and wontfix
steps: The GitHub repository has the five labels, and bug and enhancement
An issue opened from the bug or the enhancement template gets needs-triage
An accepted issue gets ready-for-agent or ready-for-human and a feature-list.json entry; a rejected one gets wontfix with the reason in the issue
features.notes: Owner action: the labels are made in the owner's GitHub account.

features.description: Branches merged into main are deleted, on GitHub and in local worktrees
steps: git branch -r --merged origin/main lists only origin/main
GitHub deletes the head branch of a merged pull request by itself
git worktree list shows no worktree of a merged branch
features.notes: Owner action on GitHub: 20 merged remote branches remain (19 claude/* and phase0-hardening). On 2026-11-07 the 21 branches merged into main were deleted on GitHub by hand; nothing deletes them automatically yet.

features.description: The network, power, time zone, hostname, firewall, log, NFS and SMART actions read and change the host through src/host.py
steps: Setting the time zone or the hostname changes them on the host: timedatectl and hostnamectl on the host show the new values
Reboot, shutdown and their cancel act on the host
Firewall rules are the host's ufw rules, and NFS exports are the host's /etc/exports
Logs come from the host's journal, and SMART data from the host's smartctl
A test fails when one of these routers runs a host command without host.run_on_host
features.notes: Today several of these commands run inside the supervisor container, or call nsenter themselves. Shared preparation for system.power, system.hostname-and-time-zone, system.logs-viewer, security.host-firewall and shares.nfs-exports.

features.description: Every data path of the supervisor follows one setting, UNOS_DATA_DIR, so the backend runs outside its container without patched module constants
steps: UNOS_DATA_DIR=<dir> starts the supervisor with its database, secrets, state files, certificates and backups under <dir>
Host paths such as /etc/fstab and /run/samba keep settings of their own
scripts/standin/run_supervisor.py sets UNOS_DATA_DIR and patches no module constant
tests/test_standin.py finds no hard-coded /data path in supervisor/src
features.notes: About 15 module-level /data paths are hard-coded today; the stand-in redirects them one by one. The health handlers in supervisor/src/main.py read /data/unos.db, /data/raid_status.json and /data/ups_config.json directly: the READ_ONLY_PROBES of tests/test_standin.py.

features.description: Changes to existing database tables ship as Alembic migrations
steps: alembic upgrade head on an empty database creates the whole schema
A change to an existing table comes with a revision, and the supervisor applies pending revisions at startup
A test runs every revision on a database made by the one before
features.notes: Today create_all only adds new tables (ADR-0077). Decide ADR-0022 before the first change to an existing table; without other installations (ADR-0207) the dev device's database may be reset instead.

features.description: The supervisor logs structured lines with level, logger and fields, and handlers log the exceptions they catch
steps: Every log line of the supervisor is one JSON object with time, level, logger and message
A handler that catches an exception logs it with its traceback before it answers
supervisor/src has no print() calls

features.description: JSON state files are replaced atomically, and a file that cannot be parsed is kept and reported instead of reset
steps: A supervisor killed while it writes a state file leaves the old or the new content, never a partial file
A state file that cannot be parsed is renamed to <name>.bad and named in a warning, and the defaults are used

features.description: Every time the API stores or returns carries its time zone
steps: Timestamps in API answers are ISO 8601 with an offset
The database stores times in UTC
The web UI shows times in the browser's time zone

features.description: The supervisor's OpenAPI schema describes every endpoint, its fields and its errors, with examples
steps: Every route of app.openapi() has a summary and a description
Every field of the request and response models has a description, and the models have examples
Each route lists the error statuses it answers

features.description: Extensions add storage backends, notification channels or sign-in providers without changes to UNOS itself
steps: A storage backend (for example ZFS or mdadm) can be added as a plugin, and one exists
A notification channel can be added as a plugin
A sign-in provider (for example LDAP or OAuth) can be added as a plugin
features.notes: Needs an ADR on whether UNOS takes plugins at all.

features.description: Two UNOS hosts share one configuration, and one takes over the services when the other fails
steps: Two hosts run UNOS against one shared configuration
Stopping one host moves its shares and apps to the other within a stated time
features.notes: Needs an ADR first; out of scope while UNOS has one dev device.

features.description: The web UI is served only over HTTPS with certificates from Caddy's local CA and with security headers; plain HTTP redirects
steps: https://<host>/ loads with Content-Security-Policy, X-Frame-Options DENY and X-Content-Type-Options nosniff
API answers carry the same headers
http://<host>/<path> redirects to https://<host>/<path>
GET /api/v1/health still answers over plain HTTP
features.notes: The stand-in serves these headers through scripts/standin/front.mjs. Device check: 2026-11-05 (Phase 0 deploy, also after a reboot of that tree); the deployed tree changed since. Open: the re-check after a reboot (ADR-0018).

features.description: Request bodies, WebSocket messages and login fields are limited before the credentials are checked
steps: An anonymous POST with a 2 MiB JSON body answers 413, and the body is not read
A signed-in 2 MiB JSON body answers 413, also when it is sent chunked
A WebSocket message over 64 KiB closes the socket
A login with a field over its limit answers 422, and audit entries store bounded fields only
File and backup uploads stream past 1 MiB under their own limits
features.notes: Step 2 is asserted only without a token (supervisor/tests/test_request_limits.py), so passes is false until a test sends a declared and a chunked 2 MiB body with a valid token and gets 413. The limit is a middleware in front of every route (supervisor/src/request_limits.py).

features.description: Sign-ins and administrative actions are recorded in the audit log, which an administrator lists, filters and exports
steps: Sign in, create a user and delete it: GET /api/v1/audit/logs lists the three entries with user, action, time and client address
Filters by user, action and time narrow the list, and GET /api/v1/audit/logs/count counts it
GET /api/v1/audit/logs/export downloads the filtered entries
features.notes: Writing entries is tested (tests/test_login_bounds.py, tests/test_audit_log.py), and so are listing, counting and exporting across the rotated files (tests/test_audit_log.py); the filters by user, action and time are not, and no page shows the log (webui.audit-log-page).

features.description: Audit entries are appended to the log one line each, off the event loop and with rotation, instead of rewriting the whole file
steps: Sign in 100 times: the audit log grows by 100 lines, and the bytes written before stay as they were
An entry is written in a worker thread, never on the event loop
A damaged line is skipped, and the other entries are still listed
The log rotates at its size limit and keeps a fixed number of old files, which GET /api/v1/audit/logs still reads

On the dev device, sign-ins append one line each to /data/audit/audit.jsonl without rewriting it (its inode and earlier bytes stay), and the SD writes of a sign-in are measured before and after the deploy (scripts/dev/sd.sh measure)
features.notes: Device check on 2026-11-07 after the deploy: three sign-ins appended three lines of about 270 bytes, the file kept its inode and its earlier bytes, and GET /api/v1/audit/logs/count counted them. A sign-in wrote 0.156 to 0.168 MiB to the SD card, 0.172 to 0.195 MiB before with a small old log; the rest is the login history's SQLite commit (architecture.sqlite-write-cost). Step 5 was reworded by ADR-0224. Not host-level (GLOSSARY.md): no reboot check needed. The old /data/audit_log.json was deleted on the device.

features.description: Each audit entry carries the hash of the one before, so an edited or removed entry is detected
steps: Every entry stores a hash over its content and the previous entry's hash
After an entry in the file is edited or deleted, GET /api/v1/audit/logs reports where the chain breaks
The chain continues across rotated files
features.notes: Builds on security.append-only-audit-log.

features.description: The supervisor bounds the size of request headers and the number of open connections
steps: The upload throughput over 2.5 GbE is measured with the HTTP parser and limits chosen, and stays at today's level
A request whose header block is over the limit is refused
Connections over the limit are refused while the open ones keep working

features.description: An administrator turns the host's UFW firewall on or off and adds and removes rules in System > Security
steps: Turn the firewall on in System > Security: ufw status on the host says active
Add a rule that allows a port from the LAN: the host's ufw lists it, and Delete removes it
The web UI, SSH and SMB stay reachable from the LAN with the firewall on
features.notes: The ufw commands run inside the supervisor container, not on the host (architecture.host-command-layer). The E2E spec only opens the section. Open: the device check and the re-check after a reboot (ADR-0018).

features.description: An administrator uploads a certificate or makes a self-signed one in System > Security, and the web UI is served with it
steps: Upload a certificate with its key and chain: it is listed with its names and expiry date
Browsers then get that certificate from https://<host>/
Deleting it returns the web UI to the certificate of Caddy's local CA
features.notes: Stored certificates are listed, but Caddy serves only its local CA: nothing hands them to the web UI container.

features.description: The certificate code keeps no special cases for files that older versions wrote
steps: The fix-ups for private keys that older versions left 0644 and for certificate names they stored without validation are gone from supervisor/src/security/router.py
Every stored certificate and key goes through the one current path: validated, and keys written 0600
tests/test_security.py passes without tests of the old cases

features.description: On a new installation the first visit creates the one administrator, and setup is refused afterwards
steps: Open the web UI of a new installation: /setup asks for the administrator's name and password
Create the account: the dashboard opens, signed in as that administrator
A second setup, also one sent at the same moment as the first, answers 400 and creates nobody
No default account exists before setup
features.notes: No E2E test covers the /setup page: scripts/standin/e2e.sh creates the administrator through the API.

features.description: A user signs in with name and password and signs out
steps: Open the web UI without a session: the sign-in page is shown
Wrong credentials show an error, and no session starts
Right credentials open the dashboard
Sign out: the sign-in page is shown, and the session's token is gone from the browser
features.notes: Step 4: auth.spec.ts 'Logout ends the session' clicks Logout and checks that the token is gone (added on 2026-11-07, after a review found the step unasserted).

features.description: A user turns on TOTP two-factor authentication and then signs in with codes that work only once
steps: On the Account page, start the two-factor setup: the QR code is drawn in the browser
Enter a code from the authenticator app: two-factor authentication is on
Sign in: after the password the code form appears, and a valid code opens the dashboard
The same code a second time is refused, and the form says to wait for the next one
Turn two-factor authentication off with a code
features.notes: The API tests cover the setup, single-use codes and turning it off; the E2E specs draw the QR code and show the code form with canned answers, but never enter a code to turn two-factor authentication on or off.

features.description: Sign-in attempts are limited to 5 per minute per client
steps: Five failed sign-ins from one client answer 401, the sixth 429
Another client can still sign in meanwhile
The sign-in page shows the 429 message
features.notes: Step 2 is asserted only as a 401 for the other client's wrong password (supervisor/tests/test_authz.py), which a lockout of the account would answer too, so passes is false until the other client signs in with the right password and gets 200 while the first one still gets 429.

features.description: Regular users see only the dashboard and their account, and every administrator page and API refuses them
steps: Sign in as a regular user: the navigation offers Dashboard and Account only
An administrator page redirects to the dashboard, and no administrator request is sent
Every administrator route of the API answers 403 to a regular user and 401 without a token

features.description: An administrator creates, edits and deletes users on the Users page
steps: Open Users and add a user with a valid name and a password: the user is listed with its role
Edit the user's role or password
A name that breaks the name rule, or exists in another case, is refused with the reason
Delete the user: the request carries the name, and a list loaded before the id named someone else deletes nobody
features.notes: The steps use a user without SMB, so they make no host-level change. For a user with SMB the same edits reach the host: shares.smb-accounts and shares.password-follows-unos cover that.

features.description: A user changes their own password on the Account page
steps: On the Account page, enter the current password and the new one: the change is confirmed
The fields are reached through their labels, and a missing field is refused
Warnings of the answer, for example about SMB, are shown until dismissed
The old password no longer signs in, and the new one does
features.notes: The tests check the answer and Samba's copy of the new password, not a sign-in with it; the E2E spec uses a canned answer.

features.description: A user creates API tokens for scripts, and a token can be disabled, expires and can be deleted
steps: POST /api/v1/auth/tokens with a name and a lifetime returns the token once
A request with Authorization: Bearer <token> is accepted with the rights of the token's owner
POST /api/v1/auth/tokens/{id}/toggle disables it, and its requests answer 401
An expired token answers 401
Tokens of another user can be neither seen nor deleted
features.notes: Untested: that a disabled or an expired token is refused. API only: no page manages tokens.

features.description: A user sees the recent sign-ins of their account with the client's real address
steps: Sign in from a client: System > Security > Login History lists it with its time and the client's address, not the proxy's
Failed sign-ins are listed as failed
features.notes: The API tests cover it; the E2E spec only opens the section, and also passes while the list says Loading.

features.description: Live data needs a signed-in session: the WebSocket authenticates with its first message, never with a token in the URL
steps: The dashboard opens /ws/v1/events and sends {"type": "auth", "token": ...} first, and stats follow
A token in the URL, a forged token or no token closes the socket with code 4401
A session that ends while the socket is open closes the socket

features.description: Each installation signs its sessions with a secret of its own, and published placeholder secrets are refused
steps: A supervisor started without UNOS_JWT_SECRET makes /data/jwt_secret with mode 0600 and keeps it across restarts
A token signed with a secret this repository once published answers 401
UNOS_JWT_SECRET set to a published placeholder stops the supervisor at startup

features.description: A user with two-factor authentication keeps recovery codes and signs in with one when the authenticator is lost
steps: On the Account page, generate ten recovery codes: they are shown once
At the code step of the sign-in, a recovery code opens the session, and the same code never works again
The Account page shows how many codes are left
features.notes: Codes can be generated through the API, but nothing signs in with one: the sign-in takes no recovery code, and POST /api/v1/auth/recovery-codes/verify answers 501. No page shows them.

features.description: An administrator requires two-factor authentication for every account, with a grace period to set it up
steps: Turn on the requirement: accounts without two-factor authentication are asked to set it up at their next sign-in
After the grace period such an account can only set up two-factor authentication

features.description: A user signs in with a hardware security key (WebAuthn) as the second factor
steps: On the Account page, register a security key
At the code step of the sign-in, touching the key opens the session

features.description: Signing out, a password change or an administrator's revoke ends a session on the server
steps: After sign-out, the session's token answers 401
A password change ends the user's other sessions
An administrator ends a user's sessions on the Users page
features.notes: Today sign-out only clears the browser's copy of the token.

features.description: The web UI keeps its session token out of localStorage
steps: After sign-in, localStorage holds no token
A reload keeps the session, or asks to sign in again, as the chosen design says
features.notes: Needs an ADR on the storage; cookies conflict with ADR-0009.

features.description: An API token can be limited to reading, or to named areas of the API
steps: Create a read-only token: GET requests work and changes answer 403
A token limited to an area answers 403 outside it

features.description: An API token's last use is stored at most once an hour, so automations do not write to the system disk on every request
steps: A script makes 100 requests with one token within a minute: last_used_at is committed at most once
GET /api/v1/auth/tokens shows a last use at most an hour old
On the dev device the requests of an automation write next to nothing to the SD card (scripts/dev/sd.sh measure)

features.description: Users can sign in while the disk that holds /data is full
steps: Fill the filesystem of /data, then sign in: the sign-in works
The audit entry that could not be written is reported in the log

features.description: Passwords are checked as given: the cut to 72 bytes kept for hashes of the passlib-era code is gone
steps: verify_password in supervisor/src/auth/utils.py checks the whole password, without cutting it to 72 bytes first
A sign-in with a password longer than 72 bytes fails like a wrong password, without a server error
New passwords longer than 72 bytes are still refused with 422, and the comment in supervisor/src/auth/schemas.py no longer points to old hashes

features.description: An administrator renames a user, and the user's SMB access follows the new name
steps: Edit a user and change the name: the user signs in with the new name, and the old one is refused
A user with SMB keeps it under the new name: Samba's account of the old name is removed, and the one of the new name is made with the password that the rename asks for
A new name that breaks the name rule, or exists in another case, is refused with the reason
features.notes: Today PUT /auth/users/{id} answers 409 for another name (ADR-0116).

features.description: The Storage page lists the host's disks with what UNOS knows about each
steps: Open Storage: every whole disk of the host is listed with model, size and serial
Each disk says whether it is the system disk, in use or holding data, and which pool it belongs to
When the disks cannot be listed, the page says why
features.notes: Device check: 2026-11-06 (slice 1 deploy; also on 2026-11-05 after a reboot of the Phase 0 tree). Open: the re-check after a reboot (ADR-0018).

features.description: An administrator creates a btrfs pool from free disks with a RAID profile, after typed confirmations
steps: Select free disks, a name and a profile: single, RAID0, RAID1, RAID1C3, RAID1C4 or RAID10, never RAID5 or RAID6
Create stays disabled until the pool name is typed, and for disks with data until the erase is confirmed
The system disk and disks in use are not offered, and a disk whose serial, WWN or size changed since it was selected is refused and the list reloaded
The new pool is mounted at /mnt/pools/<name> by UUID with a managed fstab entry and listed as healthy
features.notes: Not run on the dev device: it needs a spare disk. Open: the device check and the re-check after a reboot (ADR-0018).

features.description: An administrator unmounts and mounts a pool, and a pool comes back mounted after a reboot
steps: Unmount a pool after the confirmation: it shows not mounted, and nothing can be written into its empty mountpoint, not even by root
Mount it again: the managed fstab entry (# unos-pool:<name>) is back, and the pool is healthy
Reboot the host: the pool is mounted before Docker starts, and the apps on it start
Unmount is refused while running apps keep data on the pool
features.notes: Device check: 2026-11-05 (Phase 0 deploy: unmount, mount and a reboot of that tree); the deployed tree changed since. Open: the re-check after a reboot (ADR-0018).

features.description: Storage and the dashboard show each pool's health as the host reports it, and a degraded pool raises an alert
steps: A mounted pool without errors shows healthy
An unmounted pool shows not mounted, and one whose state cannot be read shows unknown, never healthy
Missing devices, error counters, a read-only mount and a filesystem that btrfs forced read-only are shown on the pool
Detach a device of a RAID1 test pool: within 5 minutes the RAID monitor marks it degraded and sends an alert that names the cause
GET /api/v1/health/raid-monitor/status shows the time of the latest check
features.notes: Device check: 2026-11-05 (a healthy pool, also after a reboot of the Phase 0 tree). The degraded case needs a test pool on spare disks. Open: the re-check after a reboot (ADR-0018).

features.description: An administrator removes a pool from UNOS after typing its name, and its disks keep their data
steps: Delete asks for the pool's name, unmounts the pool and drops its managed fstab entry and empty mountpoint
The disks are not touched: the filesystem is listed again as an unmounted pool that can be mounted later
A pool that host processes or containers use is refused with 409
features.notes: No E2E test. Open: the device check and the re-check after a reboot (ADR-0018).

features.description: An administrator lists, creates and deletes the volumes of a mounted pool
steps: Open a mounted pool's Volumes dialog: the subvolumes in its top folder are listed, without snapshots
Create a volume with an optional quota: it appears at /mnt/pools/<pool>/<name>
Delete asks for the name; a volume that apps, Docker volumes, shares or NFS exports use is refused with what uses it
On a pool mounted read-only the dialog lists the volumes and says why they cannot change
features.notes: Device check: 2026-11-06 (slice 1 deploy). Open: the re-check after a reboot (ADR-0018).

features.description: An administrator creates, lists, restores and deletes read-only snapshots, also on a schedule with a keep count
steps: On Snapshots, create a snapshot of a pool or a volume: it is listed with its time
Restore a snapshot: its content comes back as a new folder next to the original
Delete a snapshot
A scheduled snapshot task with keep count 3 keeps the three newest automatic snapshots and deletes no other
A scheduled snapshot of a pool that is not mounted fails with Pool <name> is not mounted
features.notes: The E2E spec only checks that the page renders, and the scheduler spec covers SMART tasks only. Open: the device check and the re-check after a reboot (ADR-0018).

features.description: An administrator scrubs a mounted pool, follows the progress and cancels it, also on a schedule
steps: Start Scrub on a mounted pool: the request returns once btrfs has started, and the API stays responsive
The pool shows the scrub's progress and, at the end, its result
Cancel stops a running scrub
A scheduled scrub task scrubs its pool, and fails without running btrfs when the pool is not mounted
A pool that is not mounted offers no Scrub button
features.notes: No E2E test starts a scrub. Open: the device check and the re-check after a reboot (ADR-0018).

features.description: An administrator reads the SMART data of every disk the Storage page lists and schedules SMART tests
steps: On Storage or System > Disk Health, open a disk: its SMART attributes, temperature and overall health are shown
Disk Health lists the same disks as Storage, NVMe included, and disks without SMART data too
A partition or another device is refused as not a disk of this system
In System > Scheduler, a SMART test task offers the connected whole disks and keeps the disk of a task while it is disconnected
Run now records the run as success, failed or timed out
features.notes: Device check: 2026-11-06 (slice 1 deploy: SMART data and a short test of the pool's disk). Open: the re-check after a reboot (ADR-0018).

features.description: SMART attributes are recorded over time, and a rising count of reallocated or pending sectors raises an alert
steps: The SMART monitor records each disk's attributes at every pass
A rise in reallocated or pending sectors sends an alert to the e-mail and Telegram channels
GET /api/v1/health/smart/trends and /smart/predictions report the trend and a failure estimate per disk
features.notes: Open: the device check and the re-check after a reboot (ADR-0018).

features.description: Disks whose SMART trend predicts a failure are marked replace soon on the dashboard and in Disk Health
steps: A disk with a predicted failure shows replace soon with the reason
The mark goes away when the prediction does

features.description: The Snapshots page lists the copies that snapshot restores made, and deletes them
steps: Restore a snapshot of a volume: the copy restore_<time> is listed on the Snapshots page
Delete it there after the check that nothing uses it: the subvolume is removed by its subvolume id
The volume that held it can be deleted afterwards
features.notes: Today a restored copy inside a volume can be deleted nowhere in the web UI.

features.description: Starting a scrub of a pool that is not mounted answers 409, and one helper starts every scrub
steps: POST /api/v1/storage/pools/<name>/scrub for a pool that is not mounted answers 409 and runs no btrfs command
The Storage page and scheduled scrubs start scrubs through the same helper

features.description: A btrfs or smartctl command that hangs in the kernel no longer holds a worker thread after its timeout
steps: A scrub, stats reset or SMART test command that does not return is killed at its timeout, and its worker thread is free at once
The API answers the timeout, and later requests are served

features.description: Storage operations stay correct with rare names, races and Docker states
steps: A subvolume renamed while the quota rollback guard runs is never taken for the new volume
Odd subvolume names, line breaks included, cannot confuse what UNOS reads from btrfs subvolume list
When Docker cannot be asked during an unmount, a Docker volume's mount of the pool is not taken for the administrator's own mount
Docker volumes are compared with bind folders after resolving symlinks and relative paths, also for third-party volume drivers
Whole disks named like xvdaa, sdaaa or dasda are accepted wherever they are listed
A failing subvolume list right after a volume create answers that the volume exists without its quota, and a create whose name was taken meanwhile names what is there
Renaming or moving a folder that is a bind mount answers 409, not 500
A folder delete stops at a mount or subvolume that appears below the folder while it is deleted
features.notes: Low-severity cases deferred in slice 1; each step can be a pass of its own.

features.description: Idle data disks spin down after a timeout set per disk
steps: Set an idle timeout for a data disk: it spins down after that time without access
The system disk cannot be given a timeout
Storage shows whether each disk sleeps, and reading SMART data does not wake it

features.description: Storage shows how much of its quota each volume uses, and alerts at set levels
steps: The Volumes dialog shows each volume's use against its quota
Crossing 80, 90 or 95 percent sends an alert
A graph shows the use over time

features.description: An administrator adds a disk to a pool or removes one, after typed confirmations
steps: Add a free disk to a pool: the pool grows, and its profile is kept
Remove a disk: its data moves to the other disks first, and a removal the profile cannot survive is refused

features.description: An administrator balances a pool and follows, pauses, resumes or cancels the balance
steps: Start a balance: the pool shows its progress and the estimated time left
Pause, resume and cancel act on the running balance

features.description: A disk attached after the supervisor started appears on the Storage page
steps: Attach a USB disk while UNOS runs: Storage lists it within a minute, without a restart

features.description: An administrator creates an SMB share on a folder inside a pool that UNOS manages
steps: On Shares, Add SMB share offers only folders and volumes of managed pools, never a pool root, apps/ or .snapshots
A new folder is made as root:unos-smb 2770, only below folders that only root can change; below a pool root that others can write, the request answers 409 and names the chmod
A folder that overlaps another share is refused
The share is served at once: smbclient lists it for a user with access
features.notes: Device check: 2026-11-07 (slice 2 deploy: a share on an existing folder, and a new folder below the 0777 pool root refused). Open: the re-check after a reboot (ADR-0018).

features.description: An administrator gives a user read-only or read-write access to an SMB share, and lowering it ends the user's open connections
steps: In the share's access list, pick a user who is not an administrator and a level
With read access the user lists and reads files over SMB, and writes are refused
With read-write access the user creates and changes files, and new files belong to the group unos-smb
Lowering the access during an open session makes the next write fail; removing it ends the tree connect
New users have no access to any share
features.notes: Device check: 2026-11-07 (slice 2 deploy: read and write over a signed session, a downgrade and a revocation during open sessions). Open: the re-check after a reboot (ADR-0018).

features.description: SMB refuses anonymous and wrong-password sign-ins while no share is guest-accessible
steps: An anonymous smbclient session is refused
A wrong password answers NT_STATUS_LOGON_FAILURE, never a guest session
With no guest share, server signing is mandatory and the guest-related globals are off
features.notes: Device check: 2026-11-07 (slice 2 deploy). Open: the re-check after a reboot (ADR-0018).

features.description: An administrator makes a share guest-accessible; guests read it and never write
steps: Check guest access for a share: the dialog warns, and so does the answer
An anonymous smbclient session lists and reads the share, and writes are refused
Removing the last guest share makes signing mandatory again
features.notes: The slice 2 device checks made no guest share. Open: the device check and the re-check after a reboot (ADR-0018).

features.description: UNOS alone writes /etc/samba/smb.conf from its database with a hardened [global] section, and the Shares page shows the SMB status
steps: After any share change smb.conf starts with the UNOS header and holds [global] and one section per served share
testparm accepts each rendered file before it is installed atomically, and Samba reloads it
A restart of the supervisor changes no file when nothing changed
Share sections that UNOS did not write are copied to smb.conf.unos-replaced and reported before an apply
The status panel on Shares shows whether Samba runs UNOS's smb.conf, and every problem as an alert
features.notes: Device check: 2026-11-07 (slice 2 deploy: the device's testparm accepted the rendered files, a restart changed no file). Open: the re-check after a reboot (ADR-0018).

features.description: On its first start UNOS imports the host's existing smb.conf once, and the import only narrows access
steps: The shares of the existing smb.conf are imported once, without guest access, and the old file is kept as smb.conf.unos-import-backup with mode 0600
Options UNOS does not support are dropped and listed in the import notes on Shares
Imported shares that break a rule are kept as not served and without access until their folder is changed
Import notes can be dismissed
features.notes: Device check: 2026-11-07 (slice 2 deploy: the old smb.conf imported, the share DATA not served). Open: the re-check after a reboot (ADR-0018).

features.description: An administrator edits a share with only the changed fields and deletes a share while its folder stays
steps: Change a share's comment: PATCH /api/v1/shares/smb/<name> sends the comment and the expected version only
When the share changed meanwhile the save answers 409, and the dialog shows the share as it is now
A share that is not served gets access only together with a new folder
Delete asks first; the share's section leaves smb.conf, and its folder stays with its files
features.notes: Device check: 2026-11-07 (slice 2 deploy: access changed with PATCH, the test share deleted and its folder kept). Open: the re-check after a reboot (ADR-0018).

features.description: An administrator runs Repair permissions on a share so that its existing files get the group unos-smb with group read and write
steps: Repair permissions on a share: its files and folders get the group unos-smb, group read and write, and setgid on folders
App data, snapshots, mounts, links and files private to their owner are left alone
ACL entries stay, and the group permissions become the ACL's mask
Shares shows the last run with its counts and errors
A share that is not served cannot be repaired
features.notes: Open: the device check and the re-check after a reboot (ADR-0018).

features.description: An administrator allows SMB for a regular user, whose SMB account is a marked host account
steps: On Users, allow SMB for a regular user: the SMB column shows it
At activation UNOS makes the host account (uid 70000-79999, group unos-smb, no login shell, GECOS UNOS SMB user) and its passdb entry
Administrators can never use SMB
Deleting the user removes the host account and its passdb entry
features.notes: Device check: 2026-11-07 (slice 2 deploy: a temporary account made and removed). Open: the re-check after a reboot (ADR-0018).

features.description: A regular user turns SMB on with their password, and their two-factor code if they have one, on the Account page
steps: The Account page shows why SMB is off, or that it is allowed
Enter the current password, and a two-factor code newer than the sign-in's: SMB is on
A password SMB cannot use (under 8 characters, over 72 bytes, control characters) is refused with the reason
Turn SMB off again on the same card
features.notes: The user's own activation ran only on the stand-in, which has no Samba; on the device an administrator turned SMB on. Open: the device check and the re-check after a reboot (ADR-0018).

features.description: The SMB password is the UNOS password: each change of it changes Samba's copy and ends the account's open sessions
steps: An administrator sets a new password for a user with SMB on: the old password stops working over SMB, and the new one works
The account's open SMB sessions end at the change
No password appears on a command line, in a log, an error or an answer
features.notes: Device check: 2026-11-07 (slice 2 deploy: a password change during an open session). Open: the re-check after a reboot (ADR-0018).

features.description: The Account page shows the shares a user can use and how to connect from Windows, macOS and Linux
steps: An active account sees its shares with their access level
How to connect shows the address for Windows, macOS and Linux, and the ipv6-literal.net form when the page was opened by an IPv6 address
features.notes: The specs answer GET /auth/me/smb with canned data; tests/test_smb_accounts.py (test_status_of_the_account_page) checks that answer on the server. The steps only read: the SMB state shown comes from the database (supervisor/src/shares/account_state.py), so they make no host-level change and need no device check. Turning SMB on and off there is shares.self-activation.

features.description: An administrator exports a pool folder over NFS to a client network and removes the export
steps: On Shares > NFS, add an export of a pool folder for a client network: the host's /etc/exports lists it, and the host's exportfs applies it
A client in that network mounts it, read-only or read-write as set
Delete removes the line and unexports the folder
Lines of /etc/exports that UNOS did not write are kept as they are
features.notes: The exports are written to the supervisor container's own /etc/exports, and exportfs runs there: nothing reaches the host yet (architecture.host-command-layer). The E2E spec only opens the tab. Open: the device check and the re-check after a reboot (ADR-0018).

features.description: After a restore, SMB stays on only for users whose password did not change since the backup
steps: Restore a backup on the dev device: smb.conf is rendered from the restored database, never taken from the archive
Users whose password is still the one of the backup keep SMB on; the others need their password again
Restored rows never take a uid that a live or a stale account holds
features.notes: Restores ran only on the stand-in, which has no Samba. Open: the device check and the re-check after a reboot (ADR-0018).

features.description: A folder counts as safe for a share only when no ACL entry and no sticky parent lets another account change it
steps: A share folder below a parent whose ACL gives write to another named user or group is refused, with the reason
A sticky parent excuses other writers only when the share folder belongs to root
On the dev device a share folder inside a sticky folder owned by another account is refused
features.notes: Implemented and tested; ADR-0193 waits for confirmation. Open: the device check and the re-check after a reboot (ADR-0018).

features.description: An administrator gives a group of users access to an SMB share
steps: Make a group and add users to it
Give the group read or read-write access to a share: its members get that access, and new members get it too

features.description: The NAS appears in the network browsers of Windows (WS-Discovery) and macOS (Bonjour)
steps: Windows Explorer's Network view lists the NAS
The macOS Finder sidebar lists the NAS
NetBIOS can then be turned off

features.description: An administrator chooses the network interfaces that SMB listens on
steps: Pick interfaces: smb.conf gets interfaces and bind interfaces only, and smbd listens only there

features.description: A share can require encryption, serve Time Machine backups or show snapshots as Previous Versions
steps: Turn on encryption for a share: clients without SMB3 encryption are refused there
Turn on Time Machine: a Mac uses the share as a backup disk
Turn on Previous Versions: Windows lists the share's snapshots

features.description: An administrator shares a volume as an iSCSI target with CHAP authentication
steps: Create a target from a volume with one LUN and CHAP credentials
An initiator with the credentials connects; one without is refused
Several initiators can be allowed

features.description: An SMB user's password changes only through UNOS, so the password rule and UNOS's copy stay in step
steps: A password change from Windows (Change a password) aimed at the NAS is refused
The Account page stays the way to change it

features.description: A restore never gives two SMB accounts one uid, nor a uid that a user deleted before the backup had
steps: An archive whose smb_accounts holds two rows with one uid is refused
A uid handed out before the backup is never handed out again after the restore

features.description: The SMB status names the reason when smb.conf was replaced after UNOS's last apply
steps: Replace smb.conf by hand after an apply: GET /api/v1/shares/smb-status names the replaced file as a problem

features.description: Unmounting or forgetting a pool re-applies smb.conf, so its shares stop being served at once
steps: Unmount a pool with shares: smb.conf no longer serves them, and the Shares page lists them as not served
Mount it again: they are served again

features.description: Every copy of foreign share sections and every import backup is kept, not only the latest
steps: A second foreign section event keeps the first copy of smb.conf.unos-replaced
Several import backups are kept, each with its date

features.description: Samba's own writes to the system disk are reduced: daemon logs in RAM, and no passdb write for a failed sign-in
steps: On a host whose /var/log is on the system disk, smbd and nmbd log to /run/samba with a small size cap
A failed SMB sign-in of an existing account writes nothing to passdb.tdb (scripts/dev/sd.sh measure)
features.notes: Unthrottled SMB sign-ins are an accepted risk (ADR-0102); a host rate limit for TCP port 445 is one of the options.

features.description: On a host whose smbd is confined by AppArmor, a share on a new folder is served without a restart of smbd
steps: An ADR decides how, once such a host is supported: for example update-apparmor-samba-profile, then apparmor_parser -r, after every change of share paths
On a test host whose smbd runs under an enforced Samba profile, create a share on a new folder: smbd serves it at once
On a host whose smbd is unconfined, such as the dev device, UNOS runs no AppArmor tool and changes no profile
features.notes: The dev device cannot check step 2: a read-only check on 2026-11-07 found AppArmor enabled in the kernel, no AppArmor utilities, no smbd or samba profile loaded, and smbd unconfined (ADR-0162).

features.description: SMB safeguards that existed only for a rollback to an older release are removed, or kept by an ADR
steps: SMB changes are audited with actions of their own; the rule to use only actions an older release knows is gone
An ADR decides whether the startup purge of SMB rows and the copy of foreign share sections still guard against restored databases and hand edits, and code kept only for rollbacks is removed
The tests of the removed paths are removed with them

features.description: Repeated failed SMB sign-ins are slowed down or locked out, and SMB-bound passwords on a list of common passwords are refused
steps: After repeated failed SMB sign-ins, further attempts from that client or for that account are refused for a while (a rate limit or a lockout)
A password on a list of common passwords is refused with the reason when SMB is turned on with it, and when a user with SMB changes to it
features.notes: ADR-0102 accepts the risk for now. A rate limit for TCP port 445 would be a firewall change on the host (ADR-0194).

features.description: Failed SMB sign-ins are logged with the client and the account, so that a client that keeps failing can be found
steps: A failed SMB sign-in is logged through Samba's auth_audit class, with the client's address and the account name
An administrator finds these lines in System > Logs and sees which client keeps failing

features.description: Repair permissions runs as a background job, so a large share is repaired in one run that the page follows live
steps: Start Repair permissions on a large share: the request answers at once, and the job runs until the share is done, without the 240 s limit of a request
Shares shows the job's progress and its end over the WebSocket, without polling
One repair runs at a time: a second start while one runs is refused
features.notes: Today one request repairs for at most 240 s and 5 million entries; then the state is incomplete, and a new run continues (ADR-0155).

features.description: The parser of /etc/exports reads every line form that exportfs accepts and leaves the lines UNOS did not write as they are
steps: Tests give the parser of supervisor/src/shares/nfs.py every line form of exports(5): comments, continuation lines, quoted and escaped paths, several clients on one line, default and per-client options
Each line is read as exportfs reads it, or reported as unreadable and left in the file unchanged
Adding or removing an export changes only the lines that UNOS wrote

features.description: An administrator installs an app from the catalog onto a chosen mounted pool
steps: On Apps, the catalog lists the apps by category, with search
Install asks for the pool, and only mounted pools are offered
The app's data folders are made inside that pool, with no '..' and no symlinks, and placeholder secrets are refused
The installed list shows the app with the host folders it uses, and warns about data outside mounted pools
features.notes: Device check: 2026-11-07 (transmission reinstalled with its login on the pool data). Open: the re-check after a reboot (ADR-0018). The stand-in has no Docker: the catalog cards are skipped there.

features.description: The transmission app installs only with a web login, and its RPC refuses requests without it
steps: Installing transmission without USER and PASS is refused
With both, the container gets them, and its web UI and RPC answer 401 without the login
features.notes: Device check: 2026-11-07 (the RPC answered 401 without the login). Open: the re-check after a reboot (ADR-0018).

features.description: An administrator starts, stops, restarts and uninstalls installed apps, and a start first checks that the app's data is on a mounted pool
steps: On Apps > Installed, Stop and Start an app: its state follows
An app whose pool is not mounted does not start, and the answer says which pool to mount
Uninstall removes the container and keeps the app's data
features.notes: The E2E spec only opens the Installed tab, and the stand-in has no Docker. Open: the device check and the re-check after a reboot (ADR-0018).

features.description: An administrator manages Docker containers and images: lists them, starts, stops and restarts containers, reads their logs live, and pulls and removes images
steps: Containers lists every container with its state, and filters by state
Start, Stop and Restart act on the container
The logs of a container stream live over the WebSocket
Images lists the images; pull adds one, and remove deletes one that no container uses
features.notes: The stand-in has no Docker, and the E2E spec only opens the page. Device check: 2026-11-06 (images and container details listed). Open: the re-check after a reboot (ADR-0018).

features.description: An administrator sets memory and CPU limits for an app's container
steps: Set a memory limit and a CPU quota for an app: docker inspect shows them
The app's page shows its use against the limits, and crossing one sends an alert

features.description: When Docker does not answer, the app and container pages and their API say so with 503
steps: Stop Docker on a test host: the container and app endpoints answer 503 with the reason, and the pages show it

features.description: The code for apps that older versions installed under /mnt/pools/default is gone
steps: The checks and messages for apps without a pool label, whose data is in /mnt/pools/default, are removed from supervisor/src/apps and supervisor/src/health
The web UI's types and texts for them are removed
tests/test_apps.py passes without the cases of older versions
features.notes: supervisor/src/apps/router.py, apps/schemas.py, health/router.py and webui/src/lib/api/apps.ts mention them.

features.description: Docker calls of the containers API run off the event loop, so a slow pull or stop does not hold up other requests
steps: While an image is pulled, or a container is stopped, removed or listed, GET /api/v1/health and other requests are still answered
Every Docker call of supervisor/src/containers/router.py runs in a worker thread, as start and restart already do
A test with a Docker call that blocks shows another request answered meanwhile
features.notes: Only start and restart use asyncio.to_thread today. Listing and creating containers, listing, pulling and removing images, and a container's details, stop, removal and logs call docker-py on the event loop.

features.description: An app can be installed to run in the SMB group, so that it can use a share's folder
steps: Install offers to run the app in the SMB group, which sets its PGID to 70000 (unos-smb)
Such an app reads and writes the share folder it was given; an app installed without the option still cannot
features.notes: Apps run as PUID/PGID 1000 today, outside the group, which also keeps internet-facing apps out of the users' files (ADR-0160).

features.description: The App Store shows the app catalog when Docker does not answer
steps: With Docker down, Apps lists the catalog and says that the installed apps cannot be loaded
On the stand-in, which has no Docker, the catalog-cards test of webui/tests/appstore.spec.ts runs instead of being skipped
features.notes: webui/src/routes/apps/+page.svelte loads the catalog and the installed apps in one Promise.all, so a failure of either hides both.

features.description: An administrator creates a configuration backup, encrypted with a passphrase if wanted, and downloads it
steps: In System > Backup & Restore, create a backup: it is listed under a unique name, also when two are made in the same second
With a passphrase the backup is encrypted with AES-256-GCM and named .tar.gz.enc
Download saves the file with the session, and a download with an expired session leads to the sign-in page
A backup that cannot be created, deleted or downloaded is reported on the page

features.description: An administrator uploads a backup file, and malformed or hostile archives are refused before they are stored
steps: Upload a .tar.gz backup: it is checked in one streaming pass and then listed
Upload an encrypted .tar.gz.enc backup: it is stored as uploaded_<date>_<time>.tar.gz.enc and checked when it is restored
A plain backup named .tar.gz.enc, a corrupt archive and a file over 256 MiB are refused and leave nothing behind

features.description: An administrator restores a backup, an encrypted one with its passphrase, and the configuration comes back
steps: Restore a backup made in the web UI: users, two-factor settings, API tokens and shares come back
An encrypted backup restores with its passphrase and is refused without it
A restore that does not fit into the RAM-backed /tmp answers 507 and changes nothing
A second restore while one runs is refused
features.notes: The SMB side of a restore is shares.restore-keeps-smb-with-proof. A restore renders smb.conf from the restored database and reconciles the SMB accounts (supervisor/src/backup/router.py), a host-level change (GLOSSARY.md): open are a restore on the dev device and the re-check after a reboot (ADR-0018). The device checks of 2026-11-06 covered only refusals: a missing file, and an encrypted backup without its passphrase.

features.description: A scheduled backup task makes backups and keeps only the newest N scheduled ones
steps: Add a backup task with retention 3 in System > Scheduler
Each run stores auto_backup_<date>_<time>.tar.gz, complete before it is listed, and two runs at once both succeed
The fourth run deletes the oldest scheduled backup and never a manual one
features.notes: The scheduler E2E spec covers SMART tasks only. Device check: 2026-11-06 (two scheduled backups at once).

features.description: Backups of the configuration and of the pools' data are copied off the device and restored from there
steps: Configure a target: a USB disk or a second NAS (btrfs send/receive or rsync), or a cloud store (restic or rclone)
A scheduled job copies the pools' data and the configuration backups there, with a bandwidth limit and encryption
Each copy is verified, and a restore from it is tested
Configuration backups no longer stay only on the system disk

features.description: A restore checks and extracts the archive in one streaming pass instead of decompressing it into /tmp first
steps: The peak use of /tmp during a restore is at most half of what it is today
A restore still refuses every archive it refuses today

features.description: Backups refuse files that are not backups at upload, and take the host's pool entries of /etc/fstab
steps: A gzip file that is not a backup, uploaded as .tar.gz.enc, is refused at the upload instead of failing at the restore
A backup takes the pool entries of the host's /etc/fstab, or no fstab at all, never the container's file

features.description: Restores take only backups whose database holds the shares, and the import of shares from an old backup's smb.conf is gone
steps: Restoring a backup whose database has no share tables is refused with a clear message
The path that imports shares from the archive's smb.conf for such backups is removed with its tests
Backups stop carrying a copy of smb.conf, unless an ADR keeps it
features.notes: The same path also imports the shares of a backup whose database has the share tables but no import marker, from the archive's smb.conf (ADR-0142): that branch stays, so step 3 needs an ADR that settles what such a backup restores from.

features.description: Scheduled backups are encrypted, because they hold the users' two-factor secrets
steps: A backup task encrypts what it stores with AES-256-GCM and a passphrase, as a manual backup with a passphrase is (.tar.gz.enc)
A scheduled backup restores with that passphrase and is refused without it

features.description: A user browses the pools and downloads files in the file manager
steps: Open Files: it starts in the pools directory, and .. goes up
Open a folder and click a file's name: the file downloads with the session
A download with an expired session leads to the sign-in page
Paths outside the pools are refused, and symlinks are shown but never followed
features.notes: Step 3: files.spec.ts 'a download with an expired session leads to the sign-in page' (added on 2026-11-07, after a review found the step unasserted).

features.description: A user uploads files into the open folder, and a file appears only when it is complete
steps: Upload files into the open folder: they are listed once complete
Each upload goes to the folder that was open when it started
A refused, failed or cancelled upload leaves nothing, and so does a supervisor stopped in the middle
Bad folders, bad names and form part headers over 8 KiB are refused before any data is written
features.notes: The supervisor stopped in the middle of step 3 is proven on Linux only: there the unnamed file (O_TMPFILE) goes with the process, while on macOS its test is an expected failure. Run it with scripts/dev/linux-tests.sh tests/test_upload_streaming.py.

features.description: A user creates folders and copies, moves and deletes items, and nothing is overwritten
steps: New folder creates a folder in the open folder, and a bad name is refused
Select items, choose Copy or Move, open the destination and choose Copy here or Move here
An item whose name exists at the destination is neither copied nor moved
Delete removes the selected items

features.description: A user renames a file or a folder in the file manager
steps: Rename an item in the open folder: the list shows the new name
A name that exists or breaks the name rules is refused
features.notes: No E2E test renames an item.

features.description: The file manager never deletes, renames or moves volumes, other subvolumes or mount points
steps: Deleting, renaming or moving a volume answers 409 and changes nothing
Deleting a folder with a subvolume or a bind mount below it answers 409 and deletes nothing
A volume can still be copied
features.notes: Device check: 2026-11-06 (slice 1 deploy). Open: the re-check after a reboot (ADR-0018).

features.description: Uploads time out when the client stops sending, and hidden upload files left on filesystems without O_TMPFILE are cleaned up
steps: An upload whose client stops sending is cut off after a read timeout, and its space is freed
Hidden .unos-upload-<hex> files left by a stop, on filesystems without O_TMPFILE, are found and removed with the owner's consent

features.description: Folders and files that the File Manager creates inside a share are writable for the share's SMB users without a Repair
steps: Create a folder and upload a file in a share's folder in Files: they get the group unos-smb with group write (2770 for the folder, 0660 for the file)
An SMB user with write access to the share changes the file and creates entries in the folder at once
Outside share folders the File Manager creates entries as before
features.notes: Today such entries get the group unos-smb from the setgid folder but no group write, until a Repair (ADR-0155).

features.description: Items deleted in the file manager can be brought back for a while
steps: Delete items in Files: they go to a trash of their pool, or a snapshot is taken first, as an ADR decides
The deleted items can be restored to where they were
They are gone for good only after a set time, or when an administrator empties the trash or deletes the snapshot

features.description: The dashboard shows live CPU, memory, network and disk I/O over the WebSocket, and the storage overview
steps: Open the dashboard: the stats arrive over the WebSocket, and the CPU, memory and network values change with them, without HTTP polling
The storage widget shows the pools with the health the API reports
features.notes: The E2E specs check the stats socket and the storage widget, but only the labels of the CPU and memory cards.

features.description: System > Resource Monitor shows CPU, memory, network and disk I/O with their history, and the process list
steps: Open System > Resource Monitor: CPU, memory, network throughput and disk I/O are shown
The time range buttons change the history shown
The process list shows the running processes with their CPU and memory use
features.notes: The E2E spec checks the tab's headings only, and no backend test covers the monitor API.

features.description: The dashboard shows the host's CPU temperature, and the API lists every sensor
steps: The dashboard's CPU card shows the temperature of the host's CPU
GET /api/v1/system/temperatures lists each sensor group with its readings
A host without sensors shows that none are available
features.notes: No E2E test shows a temperature: the stand-in has no sensors. Open: the device check and the re-check after a reboot (ADR-0018).

features.description: System > Network shows the host's interfaces, DNS, gateway, routes and connections, and an administrator brings an interface up or down
steps: Open System > Network: each interface is listed with its addresses, state and speed
DNS servers, search domains, the gateway and the routing table are shown
Bring an interface down and up again: its state follows on the host
features.notes: The stand-in has no host network, and the E2E spec only opens the tab. Open: the device check and the re-check after a reboot (ADR-0018).

features.description: An administrator sets the host's name and time zone
steps: Set the hostname in System > General: hostnamectl on the host shows it
Set the time zone: timedatectl on the host shows it, and scheduled tasks follow it
features.notes: The commands run inside the supervisor container (architecture.host-command-layer). Open: the device check and the re-check after a reboot (ADR-0018).

features.description: An administrator reboots, shuts down or suspends the host, cancels a pending shutdown, and turns Wake-on-LAN on
steps: Reboot and Shutdown in System > Power ask for confirmation, then act on the host one minute later
Cancel stops a pending reboot or shutdown
Turn Wake-on-LAN on for an interface: ethtool on the host shows it, and a magic packet wakes the host
features.notes: Built (ADR-0232): reboot, shutdown, cancel, suspend and Wake-on-LAN run on the host through src/host.py; GET /api/v1/power/pending reads logind's ScheduledShutdown, and Cancel runs shutdown -c only while something is pending; the Wake-on-LAN choice per interface is kept in /data/wol_config.json and set again at each start of the supervisor; with UNOS_HOST_EXEC=local (the stand-in, the test stack) every power endpoint answers 503 and runs nothing; POST /system/reboot, /system/shutdown and /system/cancel-shutdown are gone. System > Power shows each answer, the pending action with its Cancel button, and the interfaces with their MAC address and an on or off button; Suspend asks first too. Proven on a fake host and with route fakes only: every step acts on the host, so the entry passes after the device check and the re-check after a reboot (ADR-0018), and reboots of the dev device are owner actions (ADR-0211). The device check must show: Reboot in the tab makes busctl get-property org.freedesktop.login1 /org/freedesktop/login1 org.freedesktop.login1.Manager ScheduledShutdown name reboot one minute ahead, and the host reboots then; Cancel empties it and nothing happens; Shutdown powers the host off a minute later; Turn on for the board's NIC makes ethtool <nic> on the host show Wake-on: g, a magic packet from a second machine on the LAN starts the host after a shutdown (whether the NIC and the board support it is unknown), and after a reboot ethtool still shows g. The host needs ethtool; the startup check names it when it is missing. The UPS monitor still shuts down only outside a container (system.ups-monitoring).

features.description: With NUT configured, System > Power shows the UPS state, and UNOS shuts the host down on low battery
steps: Configure the UPS: the battery charge, the runtime and the state are shown
On battery below the set level, UNOS sends an alert and shuts the host down
Test connection names a failure
features.notes: The monitor starts in the lifespan, but nothing tests it. Open: the device check and the re-check after a reboot (ADR-0018). In the supervisor container the monitor never shuts the host down (step 2): it starts the shutdown only when is_in_container() is false, and /.dockerenv makes it true (supervisor/src/power/router.py).

features.description: The host shuts down, and wakes, at the times set in the power settings
steps: Set an auto-shutdown time: the host shuts down then
Set a wake time: the host wakes then (rtcwake)
Idle shutdown turns the host off after the idle time
features.notes: PUT /api/v1/power/config stores these settings, but nothing acts on them, and no page shows them.

features.description: System > Logs shows the host's journal, kernel messages and log files, with filters and search
steps: Pick a source and a severity: the entries are listed, newest first
Search highlights matches and shows markup in log lines as text
The filters are comboboxes named by their labels
features.notes: journalctl runs inside the supervisor container (architecture.host-command-layer), and the stand-in has no journal. Open: the device check and the re-check after a reboot (ADR-0018).

features.description: An administrator adds e-mail, Telegram and webhook channels (generic, Discord, Slack) and sends test notifications
